statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) in every hour of the CME weekend halt; Stress 25 (moderate); Confidence 76 (high).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour of this window and Tail remains far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress stays in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the 1 to 4 September data stack. No danger window is defined.
headline: Weekend halt, hour twelve: NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%), NQ 29,491.75, VIX 14.43, hawkish Warsh repricing with the 2Y at 4.34% against a semiconductor-led Friday decline
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and does not reopen until Sunday 30 August at 22:00 UTC, so every hour of this forecast window is a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August. Pre-halt evidence was re-verified against primary sources this run and is unchanged: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent or 208.13 points, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range; VIX finished at 14.43 within a 14.13 to 14.84 range against a 14.51 previous close. The dominant Friday driver was the Jackson Hole keynote, which Reuters reported was read as hawkish: the 2-year yield rose 11 basis points to 4.34 percent, CME-implied odds of a rate increase at the next meeting jumped to about 60 percent from 35 percent before the speech, and the dollar index rose 0.6 percent. Long yields stayed elevated with the 10-year near 4.67 percent and the 30-year near 5.20 percent. The index decline was narrow rather than broad: the semiconductor complex was 0 of 7 higher with NVDA down 4.57 percent, ARM down 6.33 percent, INTC down 2.85 percent and AMD down 2.33 percent, giving back part of Thursday's post-earnings rally, while AAPL, MSFT, AMZN, META and GOOGL all closed higher and gold fell 2.88 percent. That composition is a coherent single-factor real-rate repricing with internal rotation, not the persistent one-way index structure that denies mean reversion. Growth data ran the other way: Chicago PMI printed 47.1 in contraction, the payroll benchmark was revised by -79K, and final August Michigan sentiment came in at 51.7 with year-ahead inflation expectations easing to 4.0 percent from 4.2 percent. Oil eased into the weekend, with WTI at 83.44 and about 4 percent lower on the week and Brent near 89 and about 5 percent lower, as the market reframed Iran as a sanctions confrontation rather than an imminent physical-supply threat; a Venezuela reserves agreement announced after the close adds an untested supply headline. No new weekend geopolitical escalation with fresh market transmission was found this run. Tail is therefore held at 5 across all 24 slots, with the mode normal because a closed market has no structure to classify, while Stress runs 25 to 30 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on 1 September, ADP on 2 September, jobless claims and ISM Services on 3 September, and August payrolls on 4 September. Confidence at 76 reflects a complete evidence base on levels, yields, oil, volatility and the calendar, thin only on live price path, which is a venue closure rather than a research gap; it decays gradually to 70 by the end of the window as the last live print ages.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span the back half of Friday's cash session and the first twelve hours of the weekend halt. Tail ran 11 to 13 with Stress in the low-to-mid 50s through the European and early U.S. hours while positioning built ahead of the Jackson Hole keynote. The mode turned event/whipsaw from 14:00 UTC as the Chicago PMI miss and then the keynote hit the tape, and Tail peaked at 22 with Stress at 64 in the 16:00 to 19:00 UTC block; the mapped policy state never exceeded WATCH because retracements kept occurring throughout the repricing. After the 20:00 UTC cash close the readings decayed quickly, Tail from 12 to 5 and Stress from 52 to 25, as the venue entered its weekend closure and the mode reverted to normal. One hour, 10:00 UTC on 28 August, has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. The twelve halt hours are flat at Tail 5 with Confidence stepping down from 85 to 77 purely as a function of tape age.
outlookSummary: Every hour of the forecast window falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form; Tail is held at 5 in all 24 slots, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON throughout with no danger window, and the dominant mode is normal in every slot because a closed market has no structure to classify rather than because conditions are assessed as calm. Stress runs 25 to 30 in the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates: the unresolved hawkish policy read with the 2-year at 4.34 percent and next-meeting hike odds near 60 percent, Friday's contradictory growth prints of a 47.1 Chicago PMI, a -79K payroll benchmark revision and Michigan sentiment at 51.7 with year-ahead inflation expectations at 4.0 percent, the post-close Venezuela reserves agreement, and the 1 to 4 September data stack of ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP, jobless claims and ISM Services, and August payrolls. Confidence decays from 76 to 70 across the window on tape age alone. The Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen falls outside this window, so the first observable structure since Friday, including whether any gap retraces and whether pullbacks are shallow, will be scored in later cycles on observed evidence only.
